indications: First-line pharmacological treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise in adults and children aged 10 years and older. Also commonly used off-label for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and prevention of type 2 diabetes in high-risk individuals.
dosage_and_administration: Adult immediate-release: Starting dose is 500 mg orally twice daily with meals (breakfast and dinner), or 850 mg once daily with food. Increase dosage in increments of 500 mg weekly or 850 mg every 2 weeks based on glycemic control and GI tolerance. Maximum recommended daily dose is 2550 mg per day in divided doses. Extended-release (XR): Initial 500 mg to 1000 mg once daily with the evening meal; maximum 2000 mg once daily. Must always be taken with meals to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²). Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Acute conditions with potential to alter renal function: dehydration, severe infection, sepsis, hypoxemia, or shock. Severe hepatic impairment or acute alcohol intoxication.
drug_interactions: Iodinated contrast media: Metformin must be withheld prior to or at the time of an iodinated contrast imaging procedure in patients with eGFR between 30 and 60 mL/min, and re-evaluated 48 hours post-procedure due to risk of acute kidney injury and lactic acidosis. Alcohol markedly potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism, dramatically elevating lactic acidosis risk. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (Topiramate, Zonisamide) increase lactic acidosis risk. Cimetidine and Dolutegravir increase metformin blood concentration.
side_effects: Common: Gastrointestinal distress including diarrhea, nausea, abdominal flatulence, cramping, anorexia, and metallic taste in the mouth (usually transient and mitigated by taking with meals). Long-term use: Vitamin B12 deficiency (neuropathy and megaloblastic anemia) requiring periodic serum B12 monitoring. Rare: Lactic acidosis.
critical_warnings: LACTIC ACIDOSIS BLACK BOX WARNING: Post-marketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias. Symptoms include malaise, myalgias, respiratory distress, somnolence, and non-specific abdominal distress. Immediate hemodialysis and discontinuation of metformin are required. Risk factors include renal impairment, age ≥ 65 years, radiological studies with contrast, hypoxic states, and excessive alcohol intake.
